what: the concrete stair east of the house, as one average step
where_it_stands: John, 2026-08-14. The bearing is right. The flight sits half its width south of where the photograph fit put it, and its north edge is in line with the south edge of the roof.
how_that_was_applied: cabin.js puts the roof at (-34.17, -7.03) turned 18.2 deg, 8.17 m across the ridge by 8.49 along, eaves included. Its south edge runs from world (-36.72, -1.72) to (-28.96, -4.28). The flight was moved along its own across axis until its north edge lay on that line: 0.74 m toward 164 deg, against the 0.60 half-width John judged by eye.
what_is_left_of_the_photograph_fit: only how far along the flight the foot sits. That came from tracing twelve tread edges through the front door camera aimed 11.28 deg up, and the aim was corrected to 0.81 on 2026-08-13. The bearing, the placement across the flight, the tread and the rise are all John's now, or solved against the ground from them.
not_measured: the width, taken as 1.2 m, and the difference between one step and the next, which John says is real and this does not know
steps_and_tread_are_John's: nineteen steps, tread about ten inches. Those two were never fitted.

bottom.ground_m_note: The lidar at the foot is 12.04, and the flight starts 0.09 under it. John says the bottom step looks right where it is, so it is held here and the rise is solved against it.

the_slope: John, 2026-08-14: the flight was too steep and its top step stood in the air. The tread is his ten inches, and the rise is what lands the top step on the ground with the foot held where it is. 26.7 deg, against 31.3 before.
the_ground_is_cut_for_it: The bank is convex here, steep for four metres and flat after, so it bulges 0.26 m above the straight line of the flight and buried its middle. stairCarve cuts the ground down to the underside of the treads along the flight and leaves it alone elsewhere. It only cuts, never fills.
